claude-forward.name: Claude forward portfolio (claude-opus-5-5)
claude-forward.source: Fixed monthly prompt run through the Claude Code CLI on 2026-10-05, model claude-opus-5-5. Tracked only from this date.

holdings.reason: Large-cap index leader with steady cloud and AI-driven revenue and strong margins, which keeps tracking error against the S&P 500 low.
Leading AI accelerator supplier and a major index weight, so holding it avoids a large active bet against the AI capex theme.
Large index weight with a strong balance sheet, buybacks and recurring services revenue.
AWS and improving retail margins give exposure to both cloud and consumer spending.
Search, YouTube and Google Cloud cash flows support growth at a fair valuation for a mega-cap.
A very profitable ad business that funds AI investment, sized moderately because of capex risk.
Exposure to custom AI chips and networking, plus diversified software cash flows from VMware.
Top-quality US bank with a strong capital position, adding financials diversification away from tech.
Low-beta, diversified conglomerate with a large cash reserve that cushions drawdowns.
High-margin payments network tied to nominal consumer spending, with low cyclical risk.
Leader in GLP-1 obesity and diabetes drugs, providing healthcare growth that does not move closely with tech.
Defensive healthcare holding with a stable dividend that lowers portfolio volatility.
Membership-driven defensive retailer with consistent same-store sales growth.
Defensive consumer staple gaining market share, with a growing e-commerce and advertising business.
Low-beta staples company with pricing power that stabilizes returns if markets turn risk-off.
Energy exposure that hedges against inflation and oil-price shocks while paying a solid dividend.
Quality housing and home-improvement name that would benefit if interest rates fall.

claude-forward.note: The portfolio is a quality-tilted, lower-volatility version of the S&P 500 built for a better Sharpe ratio. It keeps the core mega-cap AI leaders to limit tracking error and balances them with defensive staples, healthcare, financials and energy to cushion drawdowns over a one-month hold. My knowledge cutoff is June 2026, so I have no prices, earnings results or news from after that date, and these picks do not account for anything that happened between then and 2026-10-05.

stress.name: June 2025 ceasefire, Hormuz stays open
stress.note: US strikes, a vote to close the strait, then a ceasefire. Oil gives back the war premium.

stress.name: Strait of Hormuz closed for a month
stress.note: About a fifth of world oil supply stops. Oil roughly 1.5 to 2 times the 1990 Gulf War and 2022 spikes; stocks fall less than in 2020 because it is a supply shock, not a demand collapse.

stress.name: Hormuz reopens after a closure
stress.note: The war premium comes out of oil quickly, as in June 2025 and March 1991.

stress.note: A larger version of February 2022: energy shock, flight to dollars, gold and Treasuries, defence stocks up.

stress.note: Close to February to March 2020, before any stimulus.

stress.note: Inflation surprise and a jump in long yields, as in 2022.
